safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention absence of neck stiffness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In an acute, severe headache, documenting absence of neck stiffness helps risk-stratify for meningitis or subarachnoid hemorrhage/meningeal irritation. Omitting this negative finding can lead to unnecessary escalation or, conversely, an incomplete record that complicates safety assessment if the patient re-presents.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention no fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is a key red-flag feature when evaluating acute headache (e.g., meningitis/encephalitis), and its absence supports a lower-risk picture. Failure to document “no fever” weakens clinical risk stratification and continuity for subsequent clinicians.
